one_liner: Linktree is a list of links. Carrd is a full one-page website that can also be a link-in-bio.
pick_carrd: You want full control of design and layout, not a fixed stack of buttons
You want your own domain and a page that also works as a portfolio or landing page
You'd rather pay a small yearly fee than a monthly subscription
pick_other: You want the fastest possible setup, with just links and no design
You want built-in link-click analytics without installing anything
You mainly need creator commerce features built into the link list
rows: Low to medium: themes and button styles
verdict: If your bio link is all you need, Linktree is fine. If you want the link to feel like your own site (portfolio, commissions, launch page), Carrd gives you much more for the money.

one_liner: Wix builds full multi-page websites with stores and apps. Carrd builds one fast, simple page.
pick_carrd: You need one page: portfolio, landing page, link-in-bio, event, waitlist
You want to finish in an afternoon
Budget matters: Carrd Pro is billed yearly at a much lower cost
pick_other: You need many pages, a blog or a full online store
You want bookings, members areas or an app marketplace
You want each page to rank separately in Google
verdict: Wix is the better choice for a business site with many pages. For a single-purpose page, Carrd is faster to build, faster to load and far cheaper.

one_liner: Squarespace is a polished full-site platform. Carrd is a one-page tool that costs a fraction of the price.
pick_carrd: Your site is one page
You want the lowest ongoing cost
You like building from a blank canvas
pick_other: You need a blog, store or scheduling built in
You want designer templates for a multi-page brand site
You need built-in analytics and SEO tools across many pages
verdict: Most freelancers and creators who start on Squarespace only use one or two pages. If that's you, Carrd does the job for much less.

one_liner: Framer is a design-first builder for animated, multi-page marketing sites. Carrd is simpler and cheaper for one page.
pick_carrd: You aren't a designer and want something simple
One page is enough
You want the cheapest way to get a custom domain live
pick_other: You want rich animations and interactions
You need a CMS or many pages
You already design in Figma and want a similar workflow
verdict: Framer is for design-heavy marketing sites. Carrd is for getting a clean page live today on a small budget.

one_liner: Webflow is a professional visual development platform. Carrd is the no-learning-curve option.
pick_carrd: You don't want to learn CSS concepts
You need one page, fast
Cost matters
pick_other: You're building a large site, often for a client
You need a CMS, detailed SEO control and custom interactions
You're comfortable with box model and layout concepts
rows: Monthly per site, plus workspace plans
verdict: Use Webflow when the site is a product in itself. Use Carrd when the site only needs to do one job and stay out of the way.

one_liner: Beacons is an all-in-one creator link-in-bio with a store and media kit. Carrd is an open canvas.
pick_carrd: You care about a unique design
You want your own domain on a cheap plan
You don't want platform branding
pick_other: You want built-in digital product sales and a media kit
You want creator tools managed for you
verdict: Beacons suits creators who want commerce tools bundled in. Carrd suits creators who want a page that looks like nobody else's.

one_liner: A public Notion page is free and fast to publish, but it looks like Notion. Carrd looks like a real website.
pick_carrd: You want a designed look with your own branding
You want forms, sign-ups and a custom domain on a cheap plan
pick_other: The content is docs, a wiki or a long resource list
It needs frequent editing by a team
verdict: Use Notion for documents and Carrd for anything that needs to impress a visitor in five seconds.

one_liner: Rentry is a free markdown pastebin that people use for bios. Carrd is a visual site builder.
pick_carrd: You want images, colors, layout and a proper design
You want your page to look good on mobile
pick_other: You only need text and want zero setup
You like writing in markdown
verdict: Rentry is fine for a plain text bio. Carrd is the step up when you want your page to look like it's yours.

one_liner: Google Sites is free and multi-page but looks generic. Carrd gives much more design control.
pick_carrd: Design and first impressions matter
You want forms, embeds and analytics in one place
pick_other: It's an internal, school or team site
You need several pages at no cost
verdict: Google Sites is for internal pages. Carrd is for pages the public will see.
